title: DVB-S2: add to "decode as" for UDP
description:
The heuristic dissector doesn't always work. It is convenient to have
DVB-S2 in the "decode as" menu as well.

notes.body:
I don't think the dissector can be changed to being enabled by default. There's too many false positives.

The heuristic dissector identifies 1/256 packets as being BBFrames with a L.1 adaptation header on the basis of a single CRC-8, plus any that get identified as L.4 (also lacks a check byte, so a single CRC-8), L.2, and L.3.

If you also strengthen the heuristic somehow to reject a lot more packets (presumably just in the heuristic dissector mode, not when set by Decode As), perhaps it could be enabled by default.
That makes sense. I did not find how to enable it otherwise, hwoever, where would this be done? Is there some global setting in wireshark for that?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4059/diffs?diff_id=239096855&start_sha=ec3b7606d1523fc9dc76261566edf1803d1f687a#33d911a3a83a538e4614f859c4c5faddd6527d1b_2528_2528)
To enable it go to Analyze -> Enable Protocols -> dvb_s2_udp and check the box
Thanks. I removed this part of the change.

added 1 commit
  • f0cb2fa4 - DVB-S2: add to "decode as" for UDP
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4059/diffs?diff_id=239096855&start_sha=ec3b7606d1523fc9dc76261566edf1803d1f687a)

I understand wanting to add it to "Decode As," but as is, this still leaves it approximately the same as the heuristic functionality, yes? It will still return not dissecting any bytes if the CRC check fails for all possible mode adaptation. So this doesn't really get you too much, aside from moving ahead in line in front of all the other heuristic dissectors, I reckon. What change in behavior does this get you with captures that you use?

A real "add to Decode As" solution would, I think, have only the heuristic dissector return 0 if the CRC checks fail, but would have the non-heuristic dissector just continue on processing whilst reporting a CRC error.

Presumably the non-heuristic dissector would use the preferred mode adaptation header. Since it's being set manually, and whoever sets it manually knows what adaptation header is used, probably the best approach is to use [proto_register_protocol_in_name_only](epan/proto.h#L2433-2434) and register each adaptation header type as a different PINO. (I understand if that last part is too much for an initial patch.)

I couldn't get the heuristic dissector to work with my test capture files. First I had to disable the RTP dissector because the packets were mistakenly decoded as RTP (in this case, they are not RTP). Then, it still wouldn't work despite the CRC being correct. Maybe part of the reason is that this capture has a mix of DVB and other custom protocols sent over the same UDP port (we normally don't do this, but we want to look at broken traffic to understand what's going on, sometimes).

It makes sense to have the non-heuristic dissector continue in case of CRC errors, yes. I'll see what I can do next time I can work on this.

I don't know about the mode adaptation header. It seems convenient to just say "this is some kind of DVB-S2" and let the dissector figure it out.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4059/diffs?diff_id=258600071&start_sha=f0cb2fa4c250b6e7a3b277bb71af29aafe3145bd#33d911a3a83a538e4614f859c4c5faddd6527d1b_1989_1970)

Hi,
Sorry for the delay in reworking this. I have now changed the code so that only the heursitic dissector stops when the CRC doesn't match. The "decode as" dissector will continue dissecting using the preferred mode adaptation set in preferences.
OK, looks good to me now.

commits_data.title: DVB-S2: add to "decode as" for UDP
commits_data.message:
DVB-S2: add to "decode as" for UDP

The heuristic dissector doesn't always work. It is convenient to have
DVB-S2 in the "decode as" menu as well.

The heuristic dissector does not dissect packets where the modeadapt
cannot be detected (CRC errors or other problems). The "decode as"
dissector, on the other hand, will attempt decoding anyway, using the
preferred mode adaptation set in preferences.
